requirements.summary: 2 GB RAM works · Secure Boot and TPM off
requirements.note: The project says a 2011 ThinkPad X220 with 2 GB of RAM can run Omarchy. Secure Boot and/or TPM must be turned off in the BIOS to install. The ISO is 6.0 GiB, so the USB stick needs 8 GB or more.

page.description: Omarchy editions and architectures: compare, download official images, or prepare a USB with ROMinit CLI.
page.intro: An Arch-based desktop built around Hyprland and Quickshell, made to be changed. Pick an edition, then the architecture of the machine that will run it.
pros: A finished desktop in minutes: one ISO, five questions, then it installs itself.
Arch-based, so the package manager is current and there is no release train to wait for.
Hyprland, Quickshell, Neovim and the common toolchain are wired together from the start.
Themes restyle the terminal, bar, notifications and wallpaper in one step.
cons: Secure Boot and TPM must be off in the BIOS, and that stays off.
The installer encrypts the disk by default, and Bluetooth keyboards cannot unlock it at boot.
A 6.0 GiB ISO, so the USB stick needs 8 GB or more and the download takes a while.
Apple Silicon Macs are not supported; Intel Macs work but have known limitations.
